Claim 1: the quote supports the handover to get a Danube frontier, but not 'predominantly Magyar' or the land south of the river, so the quote only partly supports the claim. Strictly, the Magyar part is a key element and is not in the quote, so I mark it no. Claims 2 and 3 are supported by their quotes; the 'alien rule' context in claim 3 comes from the same chunk, and the quote's 'that will be so' carries it, so I accept it.
judge.label: X

output.answer: Asquith says that one of the greatest blots on the whole series of treaties is that the Great Powers did not insist, as a condition of granting these countries emancipation and autonomous rule, that they remain members of one economic unit, as they had been under the Austro-Hungarian Empire. He adds that the new states have since set up artificial barriers against one another, and that this has held back industrial recovery in the region.

claims.claim: Asquith calls the failure to keep the successor states in one economic unit one of the greatest blots on the series of treaties.
claims.quote: I very much regret—I think it has been one of the greatest blots upon the whole of this series of treaties—that the Great Powers did not insist, as a condition of the emancipation and of the grant of autonomous rule to these countries, that they, should remain as they have been—and that was the one virtue of the Austro-Hungarian Empire—members of one economic unit.

claims.claim: He says the artificial barriers the new states erected against one another have retarded the re-establishment of industrial life.
claims.quote: Probably they are all in the right direction, but you ought to have gone a great deal further, and the terrible chaos to which my hon. Friend himself bore testimony, and which he obviously deplored, which has arisen from these new States erecting against one another all kinds of artificial barriers is one of the great causes which has retarded the re-establishment of free and full industrial life in that part of Europe from which, as we now know—and we realise perhaps more than we ever have done the economic inter-dependence of the whole area—we, France and America, and all the victorious nations are suffering only in a less degree than they are.

judge.reasoning: X gets the reference's key point right: the Great Powers did not insist that the new states stay one economic unit. It correctly says Asquith called this 'one of the greatest blots', which matches his own hedged wording. Its extra point about artificial barriers holding back industrial recovery is accurate to chunk 2. Both claims are supported by their quotes.
judge.label: X

output.answer: According to Jonas Vileitis's despatch to the Secretary of State, the treaty of peace was ratified by the Lithuanian Constituent Assembly on August 6th (1920).

claims.claim: The treaty of peace was ratified by the Lithuanian Constituent Assembly on August 6th.
claims.quote: The same despatch states that on August 6th the treaty of peace was ratified by the Lithuanian Constituent Assembly.

judge.reasoning: The answer gives August 6th (1920), which matches the reference. The claim restates the quote word for word. One small slip: the quote says 'the same despatch states', so the despatch is a report Vileitis is passing on, not his own. Calling it 'Vileitis's despatch' is slightly loose, but the date is right.
judge.label: X

output.answer: In his speech of 25 November 1925, Lord Parmoor said the League had between fifty and sixty constituent Members. He gave a range, not an exact number. His other speeches in the evidence (1924 and 1926) give no membership figure.

claims.claim: Lord Parmoor said the League had between fifty and sixty constituent Members.
claims.quote: At the present time in the League of Nations there are between fifty and sixty constituent Members claiming, as they are entitled to claim, an equality in treatment and consideration under the terms of the Covenant of the League of Nations.

judge.reasoning: Y gives the correct answer, between fifty and sixty, and correctly ties it to the 1925 speech. Its added note is accurate: the 1924 and 1926 chunks give no membership figure. The quote supports the claim.
judge.label: Y
